'''Francis Michael Christ''' (born 7 June 1955) is an [[Americans|American]] [[mathematician]] and professor at [[University of California, Berkeley]], specializing in [[harmonic analysis]], [[partial differential equation]]s, and [[several complex variables]].<ref name=UCB>{{cite web|title=Michael Christ (home page)|website=Mathematics Department, University of California, Berkeley|url=https://math.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/f-michael-christ}}</ref><ref name=Notices>{{cite journal|author=Jackson, Allyn|title=1997 Bergman Prize Awarded|date=April 1997|volume=44|issue=4|pages=464–465|journal=Notices of the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199704/people.pdf}}</ref> He is known for the [[Christ–Kiselev maximal inequality]].

==Biography==
He received in 1977 from [[Harvey Mudd College]] his bachelor's degree<ref name=UCB/> and in 1982 from the [[University of Chicago]] his PhD under the supervision of [[Alberto Calderón]] with thesis ''Restrictions of the Fourier transform to submanifolds of low codimension''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=9337|title=F. Michael (Francis) Christ}}</ref> At [[Princeton University]], Christ worked with [[Elias M. Stein]] from 1982 to 1984 as an instructor and from 1984 to 1986 as an assistant professor. He was at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) from 1986 to 1988 an associate professor and from 1988 to 1996 a full professor. In 1996, he became a full professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=Notices/>

Christ was a Sloan Fellow for the academic year 1986–1987. He was an invited speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1990 in Kyoto<ref>{{cite book|author=Christ, M.|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Kyoto, 1990|chapter=Precise analysis of <math>\overline{\partial_b}</math> and <math>\overline{\partial}</math> on domains of finite type in <math>\mathbb{C}</math><sup>2</sup>{{space|1}}|volume=1|pages=859–877|citeseerx=10.1.1.467.4109}}</ref> and in 1998 in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Christ, Michael|chapter=Singularity and regularity — local and global|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=627–636|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011675000}}</ref> In 1997 he shared with [[David E. Barrett]] the [[Stefan Bergman Prize]].<ref name=Notices/> He was named to the 2021 class of fellows of the American Mathematical Society "for contributions to harmonic and complex analysis, and linear partial differential equations".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2021|title=2021 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=2020-11-02}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
===Articles===
* 1987: (with Jean-Lin Journé) "Polynomial growth estimates for multilinear singular integral operators", ''[[Acta Mathematica]]'' 159(1–2): 51–80.
* 1990: "A T(b) theorem with remarks on analytic capacity and the Cauchy integral", ''[[Colloquium Mathematicum]]'' 60/61(2): 601–628.
* 1991: (with M. I. Weinstein) "Dispersion of small amplitude solutions of the generalized Korteweg-de Vries equation", ''[[Journal of Functional Analysis]]'' 100(1): 87–109. {{doi|10.1016/0022-1236(91)90103-C}}
* 2001: (with [[Alexander Kiselev (mathematician)|Alexander Kiselev]]) "Maximal functions associated to filtrations", ''Journal of Functional Analysis'' 179(2): 409–425.
* 2003: (with [[James Colliander]] & [[Terence Tao]]) "Asymptotics, frequency modulation, and low regularity ill-posedness for canonical defocusing equations", ''[[American Journal of Mathematics]]'' 125(6): 1235–1293 {{doi|10.1353/ajm.2003.0040}}

===Books===
* 1991: {{cite book|title=Lectures on singular integral operators|series=Regional Conference Series in Mathematics, 77|publisher=American Mathematical Society|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JyT3AwAAQBAJ|isbn=9780821807286}}
